title: Dantzig-Wolfe Decomposition for Linear Programming
contribution: Textbook chapter deriving the Dantzig-Wolfe master and pricing problems of an LP from Minkowski-Weyl, recovering the compact LP's primal, dual and basic solutions, and relating the reformulation to block structure, static variables, column activation, positive edge/IPS/MMCC, Benders and flow decomposition, with four hand-worked examples.
problem_entry: The LP is already solvable, so why reformulate at all: master and pricing are derived by a mathematical reformulation instead of by construction (ch. 2), the principle is a reformulation and not a solution method, and the chapter plants the idea of a structure to exploit (pp. 1, 3, 56).
key_idea: Substitute D's extreme points and rays (Minkowski-Weyl) into the objective and A to get a master with a convexity row and z_MP = z_LP for every grouping; solve it by column generation with a pricing LP that must return an element of X; recover the LP's primal, dual (Walker 1969) and a basis; with equal bounds, reformulate only for decentralization over blocks, a fast pricing algorithm or a structure created by overlapping or redundant constraints (pp. 5-14).
assumptions: LP only, feasible with a finite optimum; polyhedron with an extreme point; rational data for integer ray scaling; block-diagonal D with linking A, identical blocks (deferred to ch. 4), polytope and cone domains, network-flow pricing, static variables, standard form for column activation, CMCFP for flow decomposition; integer programs only as LP relaxations and as Benders's MILP; no model library, four toy instances (pp. 3-6, 9, 14-22, 28, 31, 35-52).
proof_devices: Theorem 3.1 (Minkowski-Weyl) cited from Nemhauser and Wolsey 1988, its proof replaced by three ideas (finite P and R, non-empty P, two inclusions); lambda determines x but not conversely (p. 5)

dual recovery (Prop 3.1, Walker 1969): strong duality in LP and MP, dual feasibility from the pricing LP's non-negative reduced costs, and zero minimum reduced cost at the MP optimum give pi_0 = pi_d'd (pp. 12-13)
basis recovery: fix the zero-valued x-variables and re-solve the restricted LP (3.20) with a simplex-type method (p. 13)
bounds z_RMP + sum_k c^k <= z_MP = z_LP <= z_RMP from Corollary 2.1 plus the minus-infinity case and kappa^k = 1; arbitrary-dual form (3.33) = Lagrangian dual bound (Prop 3.2, p. 17)

ray normalization 1'x = 1 turns ray pricing into point pricing and reproduces the primal simplex with Dantzig's rule (Note 3.9, pp. 19-20); same normalization in IPS (p. 27) and x_do = 1 in Note 3.17 (p. 51)

column activation optimality (Prop 3.3): RLP upper bound by strong duality (3.47), Lagrangian lower bound (3.46), and a negative pricing value forces a positive non-activated variable, so J grows until the pricing value is 0 (pp. 23-24)
four-variable counterexample (3.50): at a degenerate RLP solution sigma_d is not dual optimal while the pricing LP's pi_d is (Note 3.11, pp. 24-25)
positive edge compatibility test with one random vector v: an incompatible column passes with probability zero; w' = v'A_2B^-1 computed once and applied to original columns (p. 27)

Benders master derived as the dual of the MP by a bilevel rewrite, the dual passage to a polyhedron independent of the first-stage variables, feasibility cuts from its rays and the epigraph form of the inner minimum (3.63)-(3.66) (pp. 28-30)

flow decomposition (Prop 3.4, simplified from Gauthier et al. 2014): circulation transform, reformulation over the cone of circulations whose rays are cycles (paths of G when x_do = 1), and a basis of size |A|+|S|+|D| bounds the positive paths and cycles by |A|+|N|, at most |A| of them cycles (pp. 31-33)
experiments: No computational evaluation (no test set, solver, hardware, time limit or variability). Hand-computed examples: a 2-D LP solved directly and by column generation in three RMP solves, z_RMP 2,500 then 107.5 then 7 (pp. 37-40); a TCSPP with all nine paths enumerated, then five column-generation iterations, z_RMP 100.0/24.6/11.4/9.0/7.0 and lb 3.00/-8.33/6.60/6.50/7.00 (Table 3.1, p. 44; Fig. 3.14, p. 46); column activation on the same TCSPP in four iterations, x34 and x45 never activated (p. 56). Negative results reported: lower bounds that fall (p. 45), a non-optimal dual (pp. 24-25), an equality of master solutions called coincidental in general (p. 46).
positioning: Lineage Minkowski-Weyl (Nemhauser-Wolsey, Schrijver), Dantzig-Wolfe 1960/61 and Dantzig 1963 for decentralization, Dantzig-Thapa 2003, Walker 1969, Benders 1962 and Van Slyke-Wets 1969, Ahuja et al. 1993; section 3.4 reports the authors' own school: Montreal positive edge, IPS, DCA and ISUD, Gauthier-Desrosiers 2022, and Gauthier et al. 2014/2015/2016/2018, which match by year and subject the Gauthier-Desrosiers-Lübbecke papers S039, S038, S049 and S044 [inferred]; predecessors restated, not attacked; Benders with integer subproblems only surveyed; GCG and SCIP not named; Fig. 3.22 prints Forrest's 2015 decision to ship positive edge in Clp off by default (Forrest's practice, context for H7, not Lübbecke's) (pp. 5, 11-13, 27-31, 40, 56-58, 68).
writing: Joint textbook voice: Xunzi epigraph, a figure of Lübbecke drawing a polytope for two children, photographs and two reproduced e-mail threads; 19 numbered Notes, several with playful titles; a short boxed lesson and the same five-step recipe in every example; core / Good to Know / More to Know layers; hedges where the reader could over-read; one cited theorem and four proved propositions; 17 exercises with history and redo-with-a-twist items; Lübbecke's single voice only in his 2020 e-mail to Walker about listing all first names (pp. 1, 4, 6, 17-22, 34-35, 46, 56-62).
limits_future: LP only: integrality and non-equivalent groupings deferred to ch. 4, branching to ch. 7, identical blocks to section 4.4; an unbounded pricing LP returns an arbitrary negative ray; heuristic pricing gives a bound only from under-approximations; column activation pays only if few variables activate and z_LP is close to z_ILP; Benders with integer subproblems left to the literature; future: ch. 6 Lagrangian view and stabilization, ch. 7 ray scaling as a performance matter (pp. 6, 11, 14, 17, 22, 43, 56-58).

method_links.note: Steps 1, 3 and 6. Master and pricing are derived from the compact LP, not built by construction; the intuitive SDVSP pricing problem must be derived mathematically and neither of two compact formulations yields it (step 1). The compact LP's primal (3.19), dual (Prop 3.1) and a basis (3.20) are recovered, the x-lambda link is kept for this, and the five-step recipe ends in the compact formulation's primal-dual solution (step 6). A pricing structure with a specialized algorithm is a reason to reformulate (step 3). Column activation solves the compact LP itself. Taste G4: the chapter plants the idea of a structure to exploit, with decentralization as the historical motive. Also H1: partial pricing over a fraction of the blocks chosen by past success, staleness or the convexity dual, and bounds under heuristic pricing only from under-approximations.

In LP no grouping can change the bound (3.21), yet the chapter names three reasons to reformulate: decentralization, a fast pricing algorithm and created structure. SKILL.md's stop rule ties the go decision to a bound gain; the LP chapter treats reformulation as worthwhile without one. Same variant as the S084 card.

Enumeration as a teaching check, not a research instrument: all extreme points and rays of the 2-D example and all nine TCSPP paths are enumerated, the MP is solved directly and column generation is checked against it; a direct solution is possible only when everything can be enumerated; the extreme groupings (all constraints in D or none) are limit cases; no automate or prove exit.

Step 6 only (no evaluation, steps 1-5 do not apply): an equality of master solutions called coincidental and practically irrelevant in general before it is explained for this case (Note 3.16); the partial-pricing predictor called optimistic (Note 3.7); the conditions under which column activation pays (Note 3.10); a one-instance iteration count reported without generalization.

One notation re-derives column generation, the Lagrangian bound, the primal simplex, positive edge, IPS, MMCC, Benders and flow decomposition; his 2014-2018 LP-degeneracy papers with Gauthier and Desrosiers [inferred match: S039, S038, S049, S044] are folded in, Prop 3.4 being a simplified version of Gauthier et al. 2014; taken-for-granted points are written out as questions (the intuitive pricing problem, coinciding master solutions, a non-optimal dual, principle versus algorithm); step 6 credit: a full-name bibliography with middle names collected by personal exchange and corrections invited, and Lübbecke's own 2020 e-mail to Walker; the e-mail also dates reference work to September 2020, consistent with the book's overrun.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Name what the reformulation buys: bound, size, symmetry or non-linear cost
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: LP case: no grouping can change the bound (3.21), so the chapter names decentralization over blocks, a fast specialized pricing algorithm and structure created by overlapping or redundant constraints as the reasons to reformulate; column activation pays only if few variables are activated and z_LP is close to z_ILP (Note 3.10).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Close paths into cycles with a return arc so that pricing runs over a cone
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: SDVSP with arc (d,o): the pricing domain is a cone, the zero point and convexity row drop, the master is the set-partitioning LP relaxation directly, and a shortest o-d path closed with x_do = 1 gives the true minimum reduced-cost ray, against the laborious rescaling of the o-d formulation; the same device carries the flow-decomposition proof, Example 3.4 and Exercise 3.13.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Pricing as an activation oracle for the compact model
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Column activation adds the positive variables of each pricing solution and their rows to a restricted compact LP, with no reformulation; optimality by Prop 3.3; on the TCSPP four iterations against five for column generation, x34 and x45 never activated; earlier use for multi-commodity flow (Löbel 1998) and cutting stock (Valerio de Carvalho 1999, 2002); tractable only under Note 3.10's two conditions.

The grouping space is bracketed by its two extremes, all constraints in D (the pricing problem solves the LP) or none (pricing reproduces the primal simplex with Dantzig's rule), and the generic framework of Gauthier et al. 2018 [= S044, inferred] places IPS and MMCC at its two ends (none or all positive variables changed); here the extremes are limit-case checks after the general construction.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: After a primal trick, ask for its dual analogue
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Benders decomposition of an LP is derived as Dantzig-Wolfe applied to the dual (the Benders master is the dual of the MP), and Exercise 3.17 restates the primal simplex, IPS and MMCC by the dual LPs of their pricing problems.

transferable: Dual completion after column generation: re-solve the pricing LP at the final master duals; its duals pi_d with pi_b form an optimal dual of the compact LP, possibly a translation of the compact LP's own duals (+29 in Example 3.2) (Prop 3.1, pp. 12-13, 43).
Basis recovery from a master solution: fix the zero-valued variables of the recovered x and re-solve the restricted LP (3.20) with a simplex-type code (p. 13).

Partial pricing over blocks ranked by the convexity duals pi_0^k (an optimistic predictor), by past success or by time since the last call; report the Lagrangian bound only when every block's reduced cost is exact or under-approximated (Note 3.7, pp. 16-17).

Normalize ray pricing (1'x = 1, or the return-arc flow x_do = 1) so that an unbounded pricing LP returns the ray of minimum reduced cost under a stated scaling, not an arbitrary negative ray (pp. 11, 19-20, 27, 51).
Static variables: keep variables that do not appear in the structured constraints in the master instead of reformulating their bounds (2n_v bounds versus 2^n_v extreme points) (pp. 20-21).

Return arc: add (d,o) to an o-d path model so that pricing runs over the cone of circulations, without zero point or convexity row, and price rays by a shortest o-d path closed with x_do = 1 (pp. 50-51, 53-54).

Column-and-row activation of the compact LP: add the positive variables of each pricing solution and the rows they touch to a restricted compact LP, Phase I start, zero or big-M duals for omitted rows, stop at pricing value 0, final duals from the pricing LP and not from a degenerate RLP (Algorithm 3.1, Prop 3.3, Notes 3.11-3.13, pp. 22-25, 53-56).
Positive edge compatibility test: one random vector v, w' = v'A_2B^-1 computed once, compatible (non-degenerate) columns flagged by w'a_j = 0, with failure probability zero (p. 27).

Support-size bound by reformulation: reformulate over a cone whose rays are the objects (paths, cycles) and count the rows a master basis needs (Prop 3.4: at most |A|+|N| paths and cycles, at most |A| cycles, pp. 31-33).

Triangulated toy instance for a column-generation code: solve the compact LP, the fully enumerated MP and the MP by column generation and check that x, the duals up to translation and the optimum agree; log z_RMP, duals, minimum reduced cost, generated column and lb = z_RMP + c per iteration, and plot z_RMP only once the RMP is feasible (pp. 35-46; Table 3.1, p. 44; Fig. 3.14, p. 46).
coauthors: Jacques Desrosiers, Guy Desaulniers, Jean Bertrand Gauthier (four-author book S017; joint voice; one passage in Lübbecke's own voice, his e-mail of 2020-09-24 to Warren E. Walker reproduced as Fig. 3.21, p. 57)

quotes.text: This is intuitively interesting but such a pricing problem should be derived mathematically.
